title: integration-warroom-takeaways-2027-11-25
body:
Integration Warroom — takeaways + short-term plan
Date: 2027-11-25 (standup + ad-hoc warroom after 2pm EST)
Owners in room: Maya (SE lead), Diego (field eng), Priya (platform eng), Owen (SRE), Rina (customer success)
Attendees: listed above + product/PM joined for 30m
Purpose: consolidate urgent items for three live-onboarding customers and list concrete, prioritized actions for next 72 hours. Keep a minimalistic decision log and escalate path.

Top-level summary (TL;DR):
- Veridian: on track for pilot cutoff; latency spike recurring under 700-token sequences, likely KV cache warmup + kernel mismatch. Temporary routing to smaller quantized variant reduced errors but increased hallucination rates slightly.
- Tidewater: model mismatch with their safety pre-filter; incoming requests getting truncated on our edge LB due to chunking setting. Patch ready (edge-config v0.12.3), needs canary and smoke tests.
- NovaCore: batch sizing misconfig on Dedicated pool; underutilized GPUs causing higher per-token bill. Autoscale policy tweak and burst windows proposed.
- ClearHealth: compliance audit items mostly cleared; one remaining item around audit log retention export format (JSON-L vs. JSON-compact). CTO asked for concrete dev ETA.

Customer-by-customer notes:
1) Veridian (priority: P0 → pilot next Tue)
- Symptom: intermittent 150–350ms p50 jump to 900–1,200ms p95 for short requests (~200–700 tokens).
- Observations: p95 correlated with cold KV cache misses and a specific kernel path on Ampere nodes. Diego reproduced locally on a test shard by toggling cache TTL.
- Temporary mitigation applied: route 20% traffic to smaller quantized variant (q4_1-ish equivalent) which restored latency but increased hallucination probability on certain prompt templates.
- Risks: switching back to default variant may reintroduce spikes. Hallucination increase flagging CS alarms.
- Action items:
  * Priya: add KV-cache warmup hook to onboarding flow (short prefix warmup) — ETA 48h — JIRA: PROSERV-4218 (assigned)
  * Owen: collect per-node kernel-selection traces and attach to PROSERV-4218 — ETA 24h
  * Maya/Diego: prepare fallback and customer comms draft explaining tradeoffs and planned timeline — ETA 24h
- Acceptance criteria: stable p95 < 450ms on representative traffic shape OR explicit customer signoff to accept moderate hallucination increase for latency benefit.

2) Tidewater (priority: P1)
- Symptom: large-chat sessions (~5k tokens) truncated mid-request; client receives partial response and retries. Client-side pre-filter rejects partial outputs.
- Root cause hypothesis: edge load balancer chunking parameter set to 1MB chunk; their long sessions exceed chunking window and our reassembly path drops headers.
- Proposed fix: deploy edge-config v0.12.3 with reassembly fix and incremental retry suppression.
- Action items:
  * Owen: stage v0.12.3 to canary for region eu-west-1 (5% traffic) — ETA 12h — JIRA: INFRA-987
  * Diego: run replay of failing session from customer logs against canary — ETA 18h
  * Rina: notify Tidewater CS and schedule a short validation window post-canary — ETA 24h
- Notes: if canary fails, rollback plan is automatic and will suppress retries for 5m while we triage.

3) NovaCore (priority: P2)
- Symptom: Dedicated pool shows low GPU utilization (~22%) but high per-token cost compared to forecast.
- Investigation: autoscale policy min_instances too high for their traffic shape (many small bursts). Continuous batching config has conservative max_batch_latency; batching windows are too short and reduce throughput efficiency.
- Proposed adjustments: reduce min_instances by 20%, increase max_batch_latency by 15ms for their model route, allow short burst windows during peak usage (16:00–20:00 local).
- Action items:
  * Priya: update autoscale policy and submit change to Dedicated config — ETA 36h
  * Maya: update customer-facing cost snapshot and projected savings — ETA 48h
  * SRE (Owen): monitor for under-provisioning alarms after change; set auto-revert threshold — ETA 36h
- Acceptance: utilization target 60–75% during peak; no increase in request error rate above baseline.

4) ClearHealth (priority: P1-compliance)
- Status: compliance artifacts delivered; one open ask on audit log retention export format. Their security team requires JSON-L (newline-delimited JSON) with canonical field ordering.
- Action items:
  * Engineering (Priya): prototype exporter that emits JSON-L in canonical order and validated schema — ETA 72h
  * CS (Rina): collect exact schema mapping from ClearHealth and confirm acceptable retention window — ETA 24h
- Risk: if exporter misses fields, we need a hotfix and re-run parts of the audit.

Cross-cutting engineering items and notes:
- Canary cadence: we are standardizing 3-step canary for infra patches (canary-5% → canary-25% → 100%) with 30m observation windows. Team agreed — doc PR will be opened by Priya.
- Observability gaps identified: per-route KV-cache miss metrics not labeled by model_variant; need to add labels for quicker triage.
  * Owen to create metrics RFC and backend change — ETA 5 working days
- Rollout safety: for short-term mitigations (routing to quantized variant) create an explicit hallucination-quality test using known prompt bank. Maya to add 100-case prompt set for each customer to check false-positive/false-negative rates — ETA 48h.
- Escalation path reminder: SE -> Field Eng -> Platform Eng -> SRE -> Eng Director (if >4h unresolved P0). Documented in PROSERV runbook.

Decisions made in warroom:
- Proceed with KV-cache warmup hook for Veridian (Priya leading).
- Deploy edge-config v0.12.3 to Tidewater canary immediately.
- Adjust NovaCore autoscale policy on a conservative timeline; do not reduce below 60% of current min_instances to avoid cold-start regressions.

Open questions / parking lot:
- How will routing to quantized variant affect long-term evaluation metrics for Veridian? Need a follow-up A/B with artifacted prompts.
- Do we want an SLA addendum for cases where customer accepts higher hallucination risk in exchange for latency improvements? Legal + CS to advise.

Action item tracker (quick):
- PROSERV-4218: Priya (KV warmup) — 48h
- INFRA-987: Owen (edge canary) — 12h
- AUTOSCALE-331: Priya/Owen (NovaCore policy tweak) — 36h
- EXPORT-CHR-77: Priya/Rina (ClearHealth JSON-L exporter + schema) — 72h
- PROMPTBANK-100: Maya (customer-specific hallucination test bank) — 48h

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Daily 09:30 standups for the next 3 days focusing on action closure (15 minutes).
- Follow-up warroom: Fri 11/26 14:00 EST if any P0s remain.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Watch for kernel-selection logs — those traces were the smoking gun for Veridian last month.
- Keep comms short and explicit: customers respond better to timelines + clear mitigation tradeoffs.
- Save replay data snapshots in s3://proserv-replays/veridian/2027-11-25 for debug.

Attachments / useful links:
- Link to replay snapshots: s3://proserv-replays/veridian/2027-11-25 (internal)
- Runbook: confluence/internal/proserv/runbook (internal)
- JIRA: PROSERV-4218, INFRA-987, AUTOSCALE-331, EXPORT-CHR-77

Prepared by: Maya Chen (SE lead)
Reviewed quickly by: Diego, Priya, Owen, Rina
